newsitem.title: USA: USDA FY98 budget $59 Bln, PL-480 cut, farm aid up.
newsitem.headline: USDA FY98 budget $59 Bln, PL-480 cut, farm aid up.

text.p: The Clinton administration proposed a fiscal 1998 budget of $59 billion for the Agriculture Department on Thursday, $2 billion more than this year.
The food stamp program, the major anti-hunger program, would gain nearly $1 billion for a total of $25.7 billion as part of the president's plan to soften the new welfare law.
Farm support spending would climb by $1.3 billion to total $6.6 billion. The bulk of the money would be spent on "Freedom to Farm" payments, set by law at $5.7 billion for fiscal 1998.

"Food for Peace," also known as PL-480 funds, would be cut by $117 million from the $1.1 billion approved for this fiscal year. All of the reduction would come from Title I, the concessional sales program used as a market-building tool.
The administration also asked for a $60 million reduction in this year's funding for Title I.
The budget assumed full funding for the Market Access Program and the new Environmental Quality Incentive Program.
Funding for the Export Enhancement Program, limited to $100 million this year, would rise to the $500 million authorized by law.
